claim: Rewarding Doubt trains a proper-scoring-rule (log-scoring) RL reward that penalizes over- and under-confidence in a verbalized confidence token integrated directly into the generation process, rather than a decoupled post-hoc confidence head.
stance_target: verbalized confidence can be trained via RL reward shaping rather than SFT
scope_conditions: factual question answering, single- and multi-answer settings
quoted_support: Unlike prior approaches that decouple confidence estimation from response generation, our method integrates confidence calibration seamlessly into the generative process of the LLM.

claim: Rewarding Doubt was trained with 4-bit-quantized LoRA fine-tuning of Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct on a single Nvidia A40 GPU, demonstrating single-GPU 7-8B feasibility for RL-based verbalized confidence training.
stance_target: single-GPU 7B feasibility of RL confidence training
quoted_support: All models are trained on one Nvidia A40 with each training run taking seven days.

claim: On TriviaQA, Rewarding Doubt achieves ECE=0.0226 and AUROC=0.8592, and the paper explicitly argues its higher AUROC versus a Trained Probe SFT baseline (which has lower ECE=0.0189) shows the RL method is more discriminative, not merely well-calibrated on average.
stance_target: verbalized RL-trained confidence cannot be discriminative (only calibrated)
quoted_support: The AUROC of Rewarding Doubt is notably higher, suggesting that although both methods offer strong calibration, Rewarding Doubt better discriminates between correct and incorrect answers.

claim: On QAMPARI (multi-answer setting), Rewarding Doubt achieves ECE=0.0816 and AUROC=0.6947, outperforming Verbalize, Sequence Probability, and Trained Probe baselines.
stance_target: RL-trained verbalized confidence generalizes across answer-set structures
quoted_support: In the Multiple-Answer setting on QAMPARI, Rewarding Doubt also outperforms baselines, achieving an ECE of 0.0816 and an AUROC of 0.6947.

claim: The paper argues ECE alone is an insufficient calibration metric because a model that always assigns moderate confidence can appear well-calibrated under ECE while failing to discriminate correct from incorrect predictions; AUROC is needed to measure discrimination directly.
stance_target: ECE and AUROC/discrimination are distinct axes that must both be reported
quoted_support: ECE does not reflect how well a model discriminates between correct and incorrect predictions across different confidence levels. A model consistently assigning moderate confidence values could appear well-calibrated under ECE, yet fail to offer meaningful distinctions between uncertain and certain cases.

claim: Rewarding Doubt generalizes zero-shot (without further fine-tuning) across model families -- Qwen2.5 (3B, 7B), Gemma-2 (9B), and Llama-3.1-8B -- consistently reducing calibration error and improving AUROC without degrading downstream task accuracy.
stance_target: RL calibration reward transfers across architectures and scales
quoted_support: Despite architectural and pretraining differences, Rewarding Doubt consistently reduces calibration error and improves AUROC across all models, without degrading downstream accuracy.

claim: Rewarding Doubt is evaluated exclusively on factual question-answering tasks (TriviaQA, QAMPARI, MedQA, CommonsenseQA) and never on code generation or code reasoning benchmarks.
stance_target: prior verbalized-confidence RL work leaves a code-domain gap
quoted_support: On MedQA, Rewarding Doubt significantly outperforms Verbalize in both metrics, while on CommonsenseQA, it achieves a comparable ECE, however paired with a much higher AUROC.

claim: The internal correlate the method exploits pre-exists untapped in the base model: without fine-tuning, models' internal states encode truthfulness-relevant information but the model cannot translate this into an accurate expressed confidence; RL fine-tuning teaches the model to surface this latent signal as an explicit probability.
stance_target: internal uncertainty signal exists prior to training; training teaches expression, not new discrimination ability
scope_conditions: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and other tested base models before/after RL fine-tuning
quoted_support: Our findings support the claim by [prior work] that a model's internal state encodes information about the truthfulness of statements, which can serve as an indicator of uncertainty. However, without fine-tuning, the model struggles to utilize this internal information effectively.
